units.text: INT. NIGHT BUS - MOVING - NIGHT
Late November.
The number 9 to the docks.
Rain.

It comes sideways down the windows in long grey threads, and the bus lurches through the empty streets of a city that has gone to bed without it, past shuttered tobacconists and streetlamps that bloom and vanish in the wet glass.
The driver's head is a dark shape against the dashboard glow.
Nobody speaks.
The engine drones.
A single bulb above the rear seats swings on its wire.
A woman in a green coat sits near the back with a suitcase tied shut with string.
She has not moved since the last stop, and she watches the other passenger the way a person watches a door that might open.
Silence.

The other passenger, a woman in a black coat with a veil pinned to her hat, sits three rows ahead and has been turning a gold ring on her finger for eleven minutes, round and round, as if the ring might eventually come off by itself and spare her the decision.
Her face is pale and sharp.
She does not look back.
She knows she is being watched.
She has known since Hanover Street.
Rain.
The bus brakes at a red light that is the only thing alive on the avenue.
The woman in black reaches into her handbag.
The woman in green stiffens and puts one hand on the string of the suitcase.
Nothing.
The handbag holds only a handkerchief.

She presses it to her mouth and says nothing, and for a moment the two of them are the same woman, a mirrored pair of shoulders hunched against the same night, the same fear, the same engine thrumming through the same wet floor.
Her phone?
No, no phone, there are no phones.
Only the clock above the driver: ten past one.
Ten past one and the docks still twenty minutes away.
You dropped something at the last stop.
units.name: THE WOMAN IN GREEN

units.text: The veil turns.
Slowly.
I did not.
units.name: THE WOMAN IN BLACK

units.text: A letter. It had your name on it.
units.name: THE WOMAN IN GREEN

units.text: She holds it up, a small cream envelope, soaked at one corner.
She does not give it back.
Silence.
The light goes green.
The bus lurches forward.
Neither moves.
Then you know where I am going.
units.name: THE WOMAN IN BLACK

units.text: I know where you were going. I do not yet know where you will get off.
units.name: THE WOMAN IN GREEN

units.text: The bus rounds a corner.
Salt air.
Gulls.
Somewhere ahead, the dark smell of the harbour.
My name is Eleanor Hale.
units.name: THE WOMAN IN BLACK

units.text: I know. I am the one who wrote it.
units.name: THE WOMAN IN GREEN

units.text: Rain.
The bulb swings.
The envelope trembles in her hand.
Eleanor does not scream.
She only closes her eyes, as though she has been expecting this exact sentence for years, and opens them again on a face that looks very much like her own.
